{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent age inclusion criterion",
      "quote": "Age ≥ 21 years at time of consent.",
      "page": 7,
      "section": "5.2 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The inclusion criterion states age ≥21 years, which is unusual and may conflict with standard adult age (≥18) or local regulations. This could lead to enrollment issues or protocol deviations.",
      "fix": "Clarify the rationale for age ≥21 or align with standard adult age (≥18) unless required by local law."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete exclusion criteria for prior therapies",
      "quote": "Received radiation therapy (or other nonsystemic therapy) within 2 weeks before first dose of study treatment on W1D1.",
      "page": 8,
      "section": "5.3 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The exclusion criterion does not specify a washout period for systemic therapies (e.g., targeted therapy, chemotherapy) other than PD-1 blockade, which may lead to variability in prior treatment exposure.",
      "fix": "Add explicit washout periods for all prior systemic anticancer therapies."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing contraception details",
      "quote": "Women of childbearing potential must have negative serum pregnancy test before dosing at W1D1 and be willing to use an adequate method of contraception (Section 4.3.2.)",
      "page": 7,
      "section": "5.4 Contraception",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol references Section 4.3.2 for contraception methods, but that section is not provided in the text, leaving a critical gap in defining acceptable contraception methods and duration.",
      "fix": "Include the full contraception requirements in the protocol, specifying acceptable methods and duration."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent primary endpoint definition",
      "quote": "Objective response rate (ORR), defined as the proportion of subjects with a confirmed objective response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR) based on Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors version 1.1 (RECIST v1.1) as determined by Blinded Independent Central Review (BICR)",
      "page": 5,
      "section": "3.1 Primary Objective(s) and Associated Estimand(s)",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The primary endpoint is defined by BICR, but the methodology section states response will be evaluated by both BICR and Investigator assessments. This inconsistency may lead to ambiguity in the primary analysis.",
      "fix": "Clarify that the primary endpoint is based solely on BICR, and specify how investigator assessments will be used (e.g., sensitivity analysis)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing trial schema",
      "quote": "This is a multicenter, open-label, Phase 2 clinical study of CMP-001 administered by IT injection in combination with intravenous (IV) nivolumab",
      "page": 6,
      "section": "4.1 Description of Trial Design",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The trial design description lacks a schematic diagram (trial schema) showing the treatment schedule, assessments, and follow-up periods, which is essential for clarity and regulatory submission.",
      "fix": "Add a trial schema figure illustrating the study flow, including screening, treatment cycles, and follow-up."
    },
    {
      "title": "Incomplete risk-benefit assessment",
      "quote": "To evaluate the safety and tolerability of CMP-001 administered by intratumoral (IT) injection in combination with nivolumab",
      "page": 5,
      "section": "2.2 Assessment of Risks and Benefits",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not provide a dedicated section summarizing the known and potential risks and benefits of CMP-001 and nivolumab combination, which is required for ethical and regulatory review.",
      "fix": "Add a section detailing the anticipated risks (e.g., injection site reactions, immune-related AEs) and potential benefits, with reference to preclinical and clinical data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing trial stopping rules",
      "quote": "All enrolled subjects will receive CMP-001 IT and nivolumab IV according to the treatment schedule until a reason for treatment discontinuation is reached.",
      "page": 6,
      "section": "4.3 Trial Stopping Rules",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not specify criteria for stopping the trial early (e.g., for safety, futility, or efficacy), which is essential for interim monitoring and ethical conduct.",
      "fix": "Define explicit stopping rules, including safety triggers and futility boundaries, and reference the DMC charter."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent age criterion with standard",
      "quote": "Age ≥ 21 years at time of consent.",
      "page": 7,
      "section": "5.2 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The age criterion of ≥21 years is unusual and may exclude patients aged 18-20 who are otherwise eligible, potentially limiting enrollment and generalizability.",
      "fix": "Consider changing to ≥18 years unless there is a specific regulatory or safety rationale for ≥21."
    }
  ]
}
